about.title: Los Banos Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Los Banos sits at a crossroads where Route 152 and Route 165 funnel commuters, farm traffic, and travelers heading toward the Central Valley and beyond. That mix of local drivers and through-traffic shows up in the numbers: recent public records count 4 injury collisions and 5 people hurt in a single year here, with reports clustering on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. If you were injured in one of these crashes, the days right after matter. Insurance adjusters often call quickly, sometimes asking for a recorded statement before you've even seen a doctor. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect you with an independent personal injury attorney in the Merced County area who can review your situation, explain your options under California law, and help make sure evidence like skid marks, dashcam footage, or witness contact information isn't lost while you focus on recovering.

whyChoose.title: Why Los Banos Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: California's Clock Is Already Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim in California, but if a government vehicle or road defect was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Connecting with an attorney early helps make sure that deadline doesn't slip by unnoticed.

items.title: Comparative Fault Rules Can Work Against You
items.desc: California allows you to recover damages even if you're partly at fault, but your compensation gets reduced by your share of blame. An independent attorney can help push back on an insurer trying to inflate your percentage of fault after a Pacheco Boulevard or Route 165 collision.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering, No Upfront Cost
items.desc: California doesn't limit non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases, and attorneys in our network work on contingency — meaning you pay nothing unless they recover money for you.

items.question: Do I really need a lawyer for a crash on Route 152 or Pacheco Boulevard?
items.answer: Not every fender-bender requires legal help, but if you were injured, the insurance company is already building its case to minimize what it pays. An independent attorney can evaluate whether your injuries, medical bills, or lost wages justify pursuing a claim. LawProactive's matching service is free either way.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer?
items.answer: It's best to avoid this until you've spoken with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to downplay your injuries or shift blame onto you under California's comparative fault rules. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a Los Banos car accident?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. That deadline can be much shorter — sometimes six months — if a government entity, like a county road crew or public vehicle, was involved. Because evidence from crashes near Route 165 or E Pacheco Boulevard can disappear quickly, it's wise to act sooner rather than later.
